Ron Weiner – Previously with Occidental Petroleum Identify and engage with solar thermal providers In Year 1 of the project, Element 16 team identified and engaged with multiple solar thermal providers that can provide heat in our temperature range about technical and practical engineering considerations for integration of molten sulfur TES with solar thermal systems. The list encompasses: 1. Artic Solar 2. Solar Flux 3. Aeroshield 4. Absolicon 5. Winston Cone Optics 6. Gossamer Space Frames 7. Hyperlight 8. Sunvapor 9. Solar America Solutions Element 16 received information about critical parameters such as: receiver design, peak thermal power, heat transfer fluid (HTF) type, etc. of the most promising solar thermal providers that can output heat in the molten sulfur operation temperature range of 100-300 oC targeted for this project listed in Table 1. Element 16 also received data for hourly variation in steam output flow rate from the Glasspoint Solar system installed at Petroleum Development of Oman (PDO) for multiple months, and the transient variations in Hyperlight solar thermal power output for a representative day. Hyperlight Energy: Element 16 conducted a site visit to the Hyperlight Energy solar thermal test location in Brawley, California and met with the team (Figure 3). This visit helped the team understand the physical layout of the solar thermal unit and balance of system. Hyperlight Energy provided a tour of the operating solar thermal system. Element 16 measured the test site for potential layout options, documented the existing equipment and foundation on-site, received feedback on potential thermal storage interconnection options, valve material selection, heat transfer fluid reservoir sizing, foundation modifications
